messages.subject: matrix for markerXmarker lod score
parts:
We are using Rqtl for trait association in RIL melon populations. 

Recently, we have started using the two-QTL scans for analysing our data and predicting potential interactions. 

I use the package for creating a twoscan object. When plotting it seems the plot image is a matrix of the lod score for all markersXmarkers. When I use summary, each chromosome combinations is represented by a single line. 

My question is whether a matrix for markerXmarker lod score (considering each lod type for each model, e.g., full, additive) exists and how can I have access to these values?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: matrix for markerXmarker lod score
parts:
As described in the "Value" section of the help file for scantwo, the output of scantwo is a list with three components. The first component is a matrix of dimension [tot.pos x tot.pos]; the upper triangle contains the LOD scores for the additive model, and the lower triangle contains the LOD scores for the full model. The diagonal contains the results of scanone.


karl

messages.subject: Re: matrix for markerXmarker lod score
parts:
data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, error.prob=0.002)
out2 <- scantwo(hyper, method="hk")
names(out2)
lod <- out2$lod
map <- out2$map
lod[1:5,1:5]
head(map)

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] matrix for markerXmarker lod score
parts:
You could grab the code from the plot.scantwo function
https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/plot.scantwo.R#L114-L182

But personally I stick with the maximum value on each chromosome pair. The LOD scores can be useful in studying precision of QTL localization, but if you're trying to get at additional epistatic loci, you would need to look at multiple-QTL models with more than two loci.

karl
